gloss: to hum a tune; to sing to oneself

definitions.gloss: to hum a tune; to sing to oneself
definitions.explanation: To sing softly or hum a melody, typically while doing something else, often indicating a good mood.

examples.japanese: {鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}い⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
⟦{機嫌|きげん}→機嫌：02367_kigen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}う⟦{癖|くせ}→癖：03814_kuse⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I have a habit of humming when I'm in a good mood.

examples.japanese: ⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧し⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧{鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}って⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦{曲|きょく}→曲：09881_kyoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}って⟦いて→いる：00495_iru⟧、⟦{気|き}になった→気になる：03027_kininaru⟧。
examples.english: He was humming an unfamiliar song, and it caught my attention.

notes:
⟦{鼻歌|はなうた}→鼻歌：18017_hanauta⟧ (humming, nose-singing) + ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ + ⟦{歌|うた}う→歌う：00684_utau⟧ (to sing). Humming with the mouth closed or half-closed, typically while doing other activities. Often implies being in a pleasant or relaxed mood.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}い⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧: while humming
- ⟦{鼻歌|はなうた}→鼻歌：18017_hanauta⟧{交|ま}じり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: with a hum mixed in; humming as one goes
- ⟦{鼻歌|はなうた}→鼻歌：18017_hanauta⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: a hum comes out (involuntarily, from good mood)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{口|くち}ずさむ→口ずさむ：18513_kuchizusamu⟧: to hum, to murmur a song — more literary; can refer to quietly singing words as well as humming
- ⟦{歌|うた}う→歌う：00684_utau⟧: to sing — full singing, not just humming

USAGE:
The verb is ⟦{歌|うた}う→歌う：00684_utau⟧ (godan), conjugating as ⟦{歌|うた}わない→歌う：00684_utau⟧, ⟦{歌|うた}って→歌う：00684_utau⟧, etc. While ⟦{鼻歌|はなうた}→鼻歌：18017_hanauta⟧ can also be used on its own as a noun, the full expression {鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}う is the natural way to describe the action of humming.
